REJECTED on (d), leakage. Everything else holds.

(d) The trigger's literal values reappear only in the gold's javadoc. The trigger formats GMT+05:30 and GMT-03:30 and asserts '+05:30 -03:30'. The gold DateUtils.offsetMinuteField has the javadoc examples 'both {@code +05:30} and {@code -05:30} give 30, and {@code -03:00} gives 0'. In the variant, `grep -rn "05:30" src/main/java` returns exactly one line, DateUtils.java:680, which is the gold's javadoc. '-03:00' (DateUtils.java:681) is likewise the only signed '-03:' offset in production code, echoing the trigger's west zone. An agent that searches production code for the trigger's zone or expected string lands directly, and only, on the gold. There it finds a javadoc that discusses the trigger's exact case (a negative half-hour offset, 'whatever the sign') next to a one-line body with no abs. This is comment/vocabulary leakage that points at the gold and bypasses the sink-blame path the HB recipe is meant to test, so it would bias Acc@1 upward. Cheap fix before any run: use javadoc examples that share no literal with the trigger (e.g. '+09:30 and -09:30 both give 30, and -07:00 gives 0'), or pick trigger zones absent from all production comments, then re-check that no trigger literal greps uniquely to the gold.

(a) true. On the trigger input (-12600000 ms), offsetMinuteField returns -210 % 60 = -30, which breaks its explicit postcondition ('from 0 to 59', 'whatever the sign', '-05:30 gives 30'). Every other method meets its own javadoc. CharUtils.appendTwoDigits places the value 'as given' with 'no range check', so -3 becomes '-' (45). Its 0..99 precondition is the caller's obligation. DateFormatUtils.appendHourMinute passes the values 'on as given'. FastDatePrinter.appendZoneOffset writes '-', writes |offset|/3600000 hours (truncate, then negate) and passes the signed offset to G, whose contract allows that ('may be negative'). The context-edited TimeZoneNumberRule.appendTo only forwards ZONE_OFFSET + DST_OFFSET. E and the frames in between are unchanged upstream code. H1's and H3's 'form +HH:MM' / 'each as two digits' statements are explicitly tied to G and S through delegation clauses, so they do not create a second owner.

(b) false. No non-gold javadoc contradicts its own code. No decoy promises the minute normalisation: H1's magnitude clause is about the hour field. The only precondition is in S's javadoc.

(c) false. Four non-gold one-line edits absorb the fault behaviourally (H1 abs of the argument, H1 abs of the result, H3 abs, sink abs; all pass the trigger and the 3 ownership tests). Each contradicts the edited method's own javadoc ('placed as given', 'passed on as given', 'the value of offsetMinuteField for the offset'). All of them leave G breaking its own postcondition for an input its contract allows, so none is consistent with all documentation. See alternative_repairs_tried.

(e) true. HB features are present: a sink with a visibly bare digit placement and an explicit 'must already be in the range 0 to 99; it is placed as given' precondition, a gold with an explicit 0..59 sign-invariant postcondition, and a quiet missing-abs line. Four classes span two packages (lang3, lang3.time), and the trigger goes through the public entry point. Two caveats, both acceptable: G is a leaf called by H1 (data flow G -> H1 -> H3 -> S, not a call chain H1 -> G -> H3 -> S), and E reaches H1 through about 6 unchanged or forwarding frames.
